skills.skillFull: Recall the Birch reduction, in which benzene or a substituted benzene is reduced by sodium in liquid ammonia with an alcohol to give a 1,4-cyclohexadiene.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the Wurtz reaction, in which an alkyl halide treated with sodium in dry ether gives a symmetrical alkane of doubled carbon number.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the Fries rearrangement, in which an aryl ester heated with aluminium chloride gives ortho- and para-hydroxy aryl ketones.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the preparation of chloroform from propanone or ethanol with bleaching powder, via the trichloro intermediate.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the chlorination of acetaldehyde in the presence of calcium carbonate to give chloral (trichloroacetaldehyde).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the base-catalysed addition of chloroform to acetone that gives chloretone (1,1,1-trichloro-2-methylpropan-2-ol).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the dehydration of glycerol with potassium hydrogen sulfate or phosphorus pentoxide to give acrolein (prop-2-enal).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain how the oxy-acetylene flame is produced by burning ethyne in excess oxygen, write the combustion equation, and recall the approximate temperature it reaches.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the catalytic hydrogenation of an alkene over heated nickel to give the corresponding alkane.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Predict the product of the partial hydrogenation of an alkyne over a poisoned palladium (Lindlar) catalyst, which stops at the alkene stage.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the addition of bromine to an alkene to give a vicinal dibromide, and its double dehydrohalogenation with alcoholic potassium hydroxide to give an alkyne.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recognize when the product of an addition to a symmetrical alkene is a meso compound, optically inactive despite containing chiral centres.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the multi-step synthesis of sulfanilamide from aniline, via acetylation, chlorosulfonation, amidation with ammonia and final hydrolysis.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain and write the use of acetylation to protect the amino group of aniline before nitration, and the subsequent hydrolysis that gives ortho- and para-nitroaniline.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the high-temperature, high-pressure amination of chlorobenzene with ammonia over a copper(I) oxide catalyst to give aniline.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the reduction of nitrobenzene to aniline, using tin with hydrochloric acid or zinc with ammonium chloride.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the preparation of benzaldehyde from benzyl chloride by hydrolysis followed by oxidation in aqueous cupric nitrate.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the cage structure of hexamine (hexamethylenetetramine), in which four nitrogen atoms are linked by six methylene bridges.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the photochemical addition of chlorine to benzene that gives gammexane (benzene hexachloride).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the stepwise nitration of toluene with fuming nitric acid and concentrated sulfuric acid to give 2,4,6-trinitrotoluene (TNT).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the acid-catalysed condensation of chlorobenzene with chloral that gives DDT.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Define tincture of iodine as an alcoholic solution of iodine with potassium iodide, used as an antiseptic.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall where haemoglobin and myoglobin occur in the body and the biological function each performs.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Explain the essential structural difference between two similarly-named organic compounds (e.g., benzamide and acetanilide, carbolic acid and picric acid, n-propanol and isopropanol).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the molar mass, melting point and boiling point of the lower straight-chain alkanes, and the trend of these properties with increasing chain length.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Identify the classes of organic compound for which structural isomerism is not possible, such as compounds containing only one carbon atom and mono-substituted aromatic compounds.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Define a homologous series, noting that successive members differ by a CH2 unit and share the same functional group and general formula, and give an example.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall the composition, characteristic properties and uses of named alloy steels (chromium steel, cobalt steel and manganese steel).
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that amphoteric metals such as lead, zinc and aluminium react with hot alkali to liberate hydrogen gas, and write the equation.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that chlorine reacts with dry slaked lime at about 40 degrees C to give bleaching powder, Ca(OCl)Cl.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Recall that concentrated sulfuric acid oxidizes hydrogen bromide and hydrogen iodide to the free halogen, but does not oxidize hydrogen chloride.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the acid-catalysed hydrolysis of a nitrile to the corresponding carboxylic acid.
skills.subject: Chemistry

skills.skillFull: Write the catalytic air oxidation of p-xylene over vanadium pentoxide to give terephthalic acid.
skills.subject: Chemistry
